questions.question: Which of the following best defines a physical quantity?
questions.explanation: A physical quantity is a property of a body that can be measured and expressed as a number with a unit.

questions.question: A physical quantity is measured by comparing it with a:
questions.explanation: Measurement involves comparing a quantity with a standard unit of the same kind.

questions.question: Fundamental quantities are defined independently of:
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities are not defined in terms of any other physical quantity.

questions.question: In many local markets, grains are commonly measured using:
questions.explanation: In local markets, grains and similar items are often measured using cups, bowls, baskets, or bags.

questions.question: Which statement about fundamental quantities is correct?
options: They are derived from other quantities
They are independent of other quantities
They are combinations of derived quantities
questions.explanation: Fundamental quantities are basic quantities that do not depend on other quantities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Temperature is a fundamental quantity; area, volume, and density are derived quantities.

questions.question: Fundamental units are the units of:
questions.explanation: Fundamental units are used to measure fundamental quantities.

questions.question: The SI unit of mass is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

questions.question: The SI unit of time is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of time is the second (s).

questions.question: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of electric current is the ampere (A).

questions.question: The SI unit of thermodynamic temperature is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of temperature is the kelvin (K).

questions.question: The SI unit of amount of substance is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of amount of substance is the mole (mol).

questions.question: The SI unit of luminous intensity is the:
questions.explanation: The SI base unit of luminous intensity is the candela (cd).

questions.question: SI units are accepted:
options: only by engineers in one country
questions.explanation: SI units are internationally accepted standards for measurement.

questions.question: Derived quantities are obtained by:
questions.explanation: Derived quantities are obtained by combining fundamental quantities according to physical relationships.

questions.question: Which of the following is a derived quantity?
questions.explanation: Area is derived from length and breadth; mass, time, and length are fundamental quantities.

questions.question: Derived units are obtained from:
questions.explanation: Derived units are formed by combining fundamental units.

questions.question: The derived SI unit of velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is displacement divided by time, so its unit is metre per second (m s⁻¹).

questions.question: The derived SI unit of acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Acceleration is change in velocity divided by time, so its unit is metre per second squared (m s⁻²).

questions.question: The derived SI unit of momentum is:
questions.explanation: Momentum is mass × velocity, so its unit is kg m s⁻¹.

questions.question: The derived SI unit of work or energy is:
questions.explanation: Work is force × distance, so its unit is kg m² s⁻², also called the joule.

questions.question: The derived SI unit of power is:
questions.explanation: Power is work divided by time, so its unit is kg m² s⁻³, also called the watt.

questions.question: The derived SI unit of pressure is:
questions.explanation: Pressure is force per unit area, so its unit is kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.question: The derived SI unit of density is:
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume, so its unit is kg m⁻³.

questions.question: In the standard method of unit derivation, how many steps are involved?
questions.explanation: The standard unit-derivation method involves six steps.

questions.question: The unit of force is derived as:
questions.explanation: Force is mass × acceleration, so its unit is kg m s⁻², also called the newton.

questions.question: The derived unit of pressure can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = kg m s⁻² ÷ m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².

questions.question: Dimensions express a physical quantity in terms of:
questions.explanation: Dimensions show how a quantity is composed from fundamental quantities such as length, mass, and time.

questions.question: The three fundamental dimensions used in mechanics are length, mass, and:
questions.explanation: In mechanics, the fundamental dimensions are length, mass, and time.

questions.question: The dimension of power is:
questions.explanation: Power = work/time = M L² T⁻² ÷ T = M L² T⁻³.
